references.text: Concerns clay vessels that must be broken after coming into contact with a sin offering; the same principle of ritual impurity renders vessels unusable.
Nearby verses describe how clay vessels become unclean when something unclean falls into them, and how all contents become unclean.
Clay vessels touched by someone with a discharge must be broken, parallel to the rule that unclean vessels must be destroyed.
The context regarding which creeping things make objects unclean when they die and fall upon them.
The next verse gives an exception for cisterns and wells that remain clean, showing the contrast with ovens and pots.
